column3: The Hebrew uses collective singular “man of Israel” and says “to Benjamin”; BSB uses “the men of Israel” and “to a Benjamite.”
The Hebrew has singular “their voice” and repeats the weeping root in “wept a great weeping.” BSB uses plural “voices” and “weeping bitterly.”
The Hebrew introduces the speech simply with “they said”; BSB uses “they cried out.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls Benjamin “his brother” in the singular; BSB uses “their brothers, the Benjamites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes twelve thousand “men of valor”, without a superlative, and uses the image “mouth of the sword”; BSB has “most valiant” and “put to the sword”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly calls the young women “virgins” and describes not knowing a man for lying with a male. BSB conveys their sexual inexperience through the relative clause alone.
The Hebrew separately says the congregation sent, spoke to the Benjamites, and proclaimed peace to them. BSB combines these actions as sending “a message of peace.”
The Hebrew actively says “they gave them the women”; BSB changes this to passive “were given the women.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses collective singular “woman” for those destroyed from Benjamin; BSB uses plural “women.”
The Hebrew names an “inheritance” for the survivors of Benjamin; BSB renders this as “heirs for the survivors.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew commands them to “lie in ambush” in the vineyards; BSB says “hide.”
The Hebrew repeats “the daughters of Shiloh” and uses the related expressions “dance” and “dances.” BSB retains the repeated daughters but says “perform their dances.”

The Hebrew literally asks them to “be gracious to us” concerning the women; BSB expands this to “Do us a favor by helping them.” The Hebrew leaves the daughters unnamed where BSB explicitly supplies “your daughters.”

The Hebrew explicitly says they took “wives” from the dancers whom they seized; BSB calls them “women” and describes carrying them away. The Hebrew separately says they went and returned, where BSB says “went back.”
The Hebrew separately says they departed from there and went out from there; BSB compresses this into “returned from there.”
Close to the Hebrew.
